projects.name: Peskas
projects.fullName: Peskas — open-source digital platform for small-scale fisheries
projects.summary: An open-source platform that turns what small-scale fishers land and where they go into validated catch, effort and revenue data that fisheries agencies can act on.
projects.description:
Peskas is modular rather than monolithic: per-country data pipelines ingest landing surveys (KoboToolbox) and boat GPS tracks (Pelagic Data Systems), process them through a shared R library, and publish validated data to national dashboards, a regional portal, an API and a fisher-facing app.

The design point is reuse. A country joining the platform does not get a bespoke build — it gets the shared pipeline and portal configured for its fleet, its surveys and its authority. That is why the marginal cost of the next country is lower than the last.

Started in Timor-Leste and now running with national fisheries institutions in Kenya, Zanzibar, Mozambique and Malawi, with Malaysia in preparation.
partners: Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock, Fisheries and Forestry (Timor-Leste)
Kenya Marine and Fisheries Research Institute (KEFS)
DINAPA — National Directorate of Fisheries and Aquaculture (Mozambique)

projects.name: FASA
projects.fullName: Development and Scaling of Sustainable Feeds for Resilient Aquatic Food Systems in Sub-Saharan Africa
projects.summary: Making better fish feed decisions possible for smallholder farmers in sub-Saharan Africa, where imported feed is the largest cost and the biggest constraint on growth.
projects.description:
Feed is typically the dominant cost in smallholder aquaculture, and formulating it well requires nutrition data and optimisation expertise that farmers and local feed producers rarely have access to.

FASA assembles the reference data needed to answer the question — species nutrient requirements, ingredient composition, and worked formulations — and puts a least-cost formulation tool on top of it, so a decision that normally needs a feed nutritionist can be made locally with locally available ingredients.
